about.headline: WHO ARE THE MOUNTAINEERS
copy: Rich Rodriguez, 2005 to 2007. {record|33 and 5}. He put Pat White in the gun and drew up the blueprint for the spread option.
Spread them out. Read the end man. Hand it to Slaton or pull it and go, {rushyd|303 yards a game} right down their throat.

principles.title: READ HIM, DON'T BLOCK HIM
principles.blurb: Leave the end unblocked and read him. He is wrong no matter what he does.
principles.detail: We leave the end man on the line completely unblocked, on purpose, and our quarterback reads him instead of blocking him. He crashes down on the back, we pull it and go. He sits on the quarterback, we hand it off. This gives us a constant numbers advantage in the run game.

principles.title: SHOW THEM SOMETHING NEW
principles.blurb: Motion on everything. Nobody in this offense is ever just one thing.
principles.detail: West Virginia was at the front of new-age spread offense, and we are building this thing the same way: motion on everything, receivers carrying the ball, quarterbacks running power. Nobody in this offense is just one thing, and they never get to line up against the same picture twice.

principles.title: SPEED ALL OVER THE FIELD
principles.blurb: Get your fastest guys the ball in the most space you can find.
principles.detail: This whole offense only works if we have got speed everywhere, so everything we do is built to get our fastest guys the ball in the most space we can find. The play does not have to be perfect. They only need one crease.

lineage.name: MARCUS MARIOTA
stats: 42 total TD in the Heisman year
lineage.brought: The cleanest zone read trigger the scheme ever produced. Every wrong step a defense took turned into a chunk play the other way. Calm, fast, and never fooled twice by the same look.

lineage.name: PAT WHITE
stats: Won four straight bowls as the starter
lineage.brought: The original dual threat. Defenses knew the read was coming for four straight years and still could not stop it. Nobody punished a crashing end harder, and nobody made the option look easier.

lineage.name: LAMICHAEL JAMES
lineage.brought: The engine of the blur. One cut, zero wasted steps, and the scoreboard moved. Back to back seasons over 1,700 yards because the offense never let a defense set its feet.

lineage.name: TREVEYON HENDERSON
stats: 75 yd TD to ice the title game
lineage.brought: Home run speed that closed out a championship. Never needed volume, only a crease, and the 75 yarder against Texas is the proof. The best pass protecting back in the sport on top of it.

lineage.name: DE'ANTHONY THOMAS
stats: 1,890 all purpose yds as a sophomore
lineage.brought: The Black Mamba. Lined up everywhere and scored from everywhere. Space around him was a death sentence, so every defense had to find him before the snap and most of them still lost him.

lineage.name: TAVON AUSTIN
stats: 572 total yds in one game vs Oklahoma
lineage.brought: The jet motion nightmare no defense ever solved. Every yard started with the defense leaning the wrong way, and the Oklahoma tape is still the scariest game a slot has ever put out.

lineage.name: JEREMIAH SMITH
lineage.brought: The standard. Won at the catch point every single time as a true freshman on a title team, and tilted coverage just by walking on the field. Safeties rolled his way all year and it did not matter.

lineage.name: JOSH HUFF
lineage.brought: Play action cashed its checks outside for four straight years. The blur held the safeties in the box, and Huff made them pay over the top every time they cheated.

title.name: THE SPREAD TO RUN OFFENSE
title.sub: One system. Three programs. A thousand miles apart, running the same play.

teams.name: OREGON
teams.writeup: The blur years. Chip Kelly took the spread run game and strapped a jet engine to it: no huddle, no mercy. From 2009 to 2012 Oregon went 46 and 7, played for a national title, and won four straight BCS bowls out of Eugene. LaMichael James ran for over 1,700 twice while the Ducks led the country in scoring, snapping the ball before defenses could even get lined up.

teams.name: OHIO STATE
teams.writeup: The proof it still wins. Chip Kelly came back to call the plays, the spread run game set the table, and Ohio State ran through the entire sport in 2024: a national championship behind a true freshman phenom in Jeremiah Smith. Twenty years after Morgantown, the same offense is still carving defenses apart.

teams.writeup: The birthplace. Rich Rodriguez drew the modern zone read up in Morgantown and handed it to two blurs. In 2006 alone Pat White and Steve Slaton piled up 2,963 rushing yards together, and White walked away as the only quarterback in history to start and win four bowl games. Every zone read defenses chase on Saturdays traces back to here.

plays.name: MTN RPO Read Flat

reads.label: Read the Edge Defender
reads.text: Come out in Spread Y-Slot and read the edge man. If he crashes down on the back, pull it and get your quarterback out on the perimeter, and that is where he does damage. If he sits and takes the quarterback away, hand it off up the middle and get downhill.

reads.label: Flip It to the Flat
reads.text: The auto motion sends a player across to the flat pre-snap. If you pull it and defenders come flying at the quarterback, just flip it out to your guy in the flat. He has a ton of room to work in the open field.

reads.label: Everybody Sucks Inside
reads.text: If the whole defense collapses inside on the read, same answer: pop it out to the flat and let your playmaker make people miss for big plays on the edge.

adjustments: Come out with our running back to the wide side of the field.
plays.whenToUse: This is the play West Virginia was built on. Come out in Spread Y-Slot, read the edge, and take whatever he gives you. The motion to the flat buys you a free answer: pull it and get pressured, you flip it out to open grass. It is the first thing you install and the base everything else grows from.

plays.name: MTN Triple Option RT

reads.label: Read the End
reads.text: The whole thing starts with an auto motion from your slot gadget player coming across into the backfield. If the end crashes down, pull it and get out on the perimeter. Now you have a triple option working with your quarterback and your running back.

reads.label: Pitch It Out
reads.text: What you want is everybody sucking in on the quarterback. The second they do, flip it out to the running back and create huge plays on the edge.

reads.label: Hand It Up the Middle
reads.text: That slot gadget player is the running back in the read. If they are overplaying the pitch, just hand it off to him up the middle. If they are all flying outside, there are big lanes right there for him to make plays as a runner.

adjustments: Come out with the trips to the wide side.
plays.whenToUse: This is one of the best run plays in the whole scheme and it leads your run game install. It gets you out on the perimeter and creates a ton of huge plays. Everybody sucks in on the quarterback, you flip it to the back on the edge. They overplay the pitch, you hand it up the middle into open grass.

plays.name: Jet QB Power

reads.label: Sell the Jet
reads.text: The auto motion player comes all the way across and it looks exactly like a jet touch pass. A ton of the time the linebackers and the user leave the middle of the field to go chase it.

reads.label: Get Downhill
reads.text: That is when you are getting downhill with your quarterback and a puller out in front of him. You are in empty, so they are already spread out sideline to sideline.

reads.label: Nobody in the Box
reads.text: Now you have a power run coming right up the gut with nobody left in there to stop it. You can bust off absolutely massive gains with this one.

adjustments: Come out with your trips to the wide side.
plays.whenToUse: Run this once the jet motion has them jumping. You have shown them the jet touch pass, the linebackers start chasing it, and now the power hits right up the gut with a puller and nobody home. Empty spreads the box out for you first, so the crease is huge.

plays.name: QB Zone

reads.label: Box Count
reads.text: Count defenders in the box. In empty, the defense is forced to spread out with their personnel, often leaving only 5 in the box against 6 blockers plus the QB, a 7-on-5 numbers advantage.

reads.label: Man Coverage Box Load
reads.text: If the defense matches in man coverage, they can reload the box to 6 or 7 defenders. Numbers are still even, and 6 blockers plus the QB gives you at least even odds, still runnable.

reads.label: Linebacker Gap Fit
reads.text: Read linebacker flow and gap assignment post-snap. The zone blocking scheme is designed to let linebackers shoot themselves into the wrong hole, creating cutback lanes or edge opportunities.

adjustments: Come out with your trips to the wide side.
plays.whenToUse: Call this in the red zone, goal line, or short yardage when you have an athletic QB who can carry it. Empty forces them to spread their box, so you get 7-on-5 most of the time. Even when they load up in man, the numbers are still even and the zone scheme handles it. This is a West Virginia staple. If they respect your empty pass threat, they are giving you this run.

plays.name: Jet Touch Pass

reads.label: Edge Pursuit
reads.text: Read the edge defender's pursuit angle on the jet motion. If he overcommits outside, look for the cutback lane back inside.

reads.label: Box Load
reads.text: If the defense loads the box anticipating a QB draw or inside run, flip it to the edge. Everyone gets caught inside and it is a walk-in.

reads.label: Perimeter Block
reads.text: Read the blocking on the perimeter. If the linebackers are slow to react to the motion and blocks are secured, get to the edge untouched.

adjustments: Come out with your trips to the wide side.
plays.whenToUse: Start the game with this one. Get them used to seeing the jet motion, let the linebackers chase it a couple times, and bank those yards. It is money on the goal line when they load the box, everybody freezes inside and your guy walks in. Once they start flying out to stop it, that is when you hit them with jet QB power and PA jet sweep.

plays.name: MTN WR Counter RT

reads.label: Kick-Out Block
reads.text: Read the tight end's kick-out block on the edge defender. If he seals, press the hole and get vertical up the seam.

reads.label: Puller
reads.text: Follow the pulling lineman or running back as a lead blocker around the corner. Let them create the crease before committing to a lane.

reads.label: Bounce vs. Press
reads.text: If the interior hole is flowing, bounce to the outside behind the kick-out. If blockers win at the point of attack, press it straight up the seam.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field.
plays.whenToUse: When you have a playmaker, a Tavon Austin type, and you want to get him the ball downhill with a full complement of blockers. This is your gadget counter. Run it off your PA and option motions so the defense cannot key it. Perfect for when you need a big chunk play.

plays.name: Sprint Smash

reads.label: Corner Route (First Read)
reads.text: The whole thing starts with an auto rollout, getting your athletic quarterback out on the perimeter right away. First read is always the corner. If that flat defender bites back down, or it is man and he is separating, drop it in over the top for a big play.

reads.label: Deep Cross
reads.text: Once you are out on the edge, if the corner is taken away, look to the middle. If the linebackers bit down on the rollout or jumped over to help on the corner, the deep cross is working right into that space.

reads.label: Drag Checkdown
reads.text: If you try to get out on the auto rollout and the end crashes and contains you, just hold up in the pocket and hit the drag.

reads.label: Tuck and Go
reads.text: If you are out on the edge with your athletic quarterback and nothing is open down the field but you have green grass in front of you, just tuck it and run. That is a big pickup every time.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side.
Trips-side outside receiver on a streak.
Short-side outside receiver on a drag.
plays.whenToUse: This feeds right off the run game. Come out empty with trips to the wide side and let the auto rollout put your quarterback in space. Corner over the top first, deep cross into the vacated middle, drag as your checkdown, and if it all locks up, tuck it and pick up big yards on the ground.

plays.name: Flood HB Flat

reads.label: Slot Option Route (First Read)
reads.text: First read is always the option route from the slot. He gets to about ten yards. Against zone he sits down and finds the soft spot, fire it in. Against man he options out to the sideline, gets really good separation, and you rip it in.

reads.label: Corner Route
reads.text: If they have the slot covered, your eyes go straight to the corner. If that flat defender bit down on the back in the flat, throw it up over the top. He tends to get good separation against man too.

reads.label: RB in the Flat
reads.text: If the flat defender is playing way back, just drop it down to the running back in space.

reads.label: TE on the Hook
reads.text: If the linebackers leave the middle to take away that option route, the tight end is sitting right there on the hook.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field.
Middle slot receiver on a corner route.
plays.whenToUse: One of the best plays in the entire scheme, with answers for man and zone and unbelievable field spacing. Lean on the slot option route: it sits versus zone and separates versus man. The corner is your shot over the top, and the RB flat and TE hook are your clean underneath answers when they take the top away.

plays.name: MTN PA Slide

reads.label: Deep Corner (First Read)
reads.text: First read is the deep corner working down the sideline. If that flat defender bites down, just fire it in over the top.

reads.label: Crosser
reads.text: The crosser comes across the middle of the field. If the linebackers leave the middle to chase the rollout, that crosser is wide open. This one is a really good option against man too.

reads.label: Motion Player in the Flat
reads.text: If everybody is playing way back, drop it down to your motion player who came all the way across into the flat and let him make plays in the open field.

adjustments: Auto motion to the short side.
Wide-side outside receiver on a streak.
Wide-side slot on a corner route.
plays.whenToUse: The pre-snap motion here is identical to MTN RPO Read Flat, the first play you installed, so these two work great off each other. When they start keying the read, hit them with the play action: deep corner over the top, crosser into the vacated middle, motion player in the flat as the outlet.

plays.name: RZ Dusty

reads.label: Wide-Side Slant (Go-To)
reads.text: Your go-to is the wide-side slot on the slant. This is not a stock slant, it is a better version that gets really quick separation right off the snap. It is just an easy win over and over.

reads.label: Corner and Post
reads.text: Two intermediate answers: the corner route from the tight end on the wide side, and the post from your backside receiver. Both get nice separation, one attacking the middle, the other the sideline.

reads.label: Whip and Shallow Cross
reads.text: Your two underneath options are the whip breaking back to the outside, and a really unique shallow cross that gets good separation coming over the middle.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field.
Slot receiver on the short side on a whip.
plays.whenToUse: This is your go-to man beater. If they are sitting in a ton of man coverage, this is the call. What makes it so good is you have five man beaters on the field at once, so there is always a winner. Start with the wide-side slant and work out from there.

plays.name: Jet Chip Wasp

reads.label: 1st Read: Wasp Route
reads.text: Primary read. The runner goes deep cross then breaks back out to the corner, about 40 yards. Against man, the streak on the outside clears the safety so the Wasp gets one-on-one separation on the break. Against zone, the zone drop would need to be set at 30 yards to take it away, and it will not be, so drop it in over their heads.

reads.label: 2nd Read: Deep Crosser
reads.text: The tight end runs a deep cross. It works vs man and zone. The streak pulls defenders deep while the tight end drags over the flat defender's head, about 15 yards. If coverage switches onto the Wasp, the crosser gets in behind and opens up.

reads.label: 3rd Read: RB Check Down
reads.text: The running back is on a check-and-release. If the Wasp and Crosser both have coverage on them, dump it to the back in the flat and let him work in open field.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side.
TE on drag or corner vs man.
Backside receiver on a streak.
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you need a big play and you are not sure what coverage they are in, it beats man and zone. Give yourself a clean pocket, no heavy blitz look. Money play on third and long or any time you need a chunk play down the field.

plays.name: PA Jet Sweep

reads.label: 1st Read: Deep Post
reads.text: If the linebackers flow hard to the jet motion and vacate the middle, fire the deep post with anticipation. If the deep safety is playing a deep half rather than a post safety, the middle of the field opens up for an easy throw.

reads.label: 2nd Read: Shallow Drag / Shallow Cross
reads.text: If linebackers jump down or flow to the jet motion in zone or man, the shallow drag or crossing route comes in behind them. Works especially well in the red zone when defenders aggressively pursue the fake.

reads.label: 3rd Read: Tight End Underneath
reads.text: If the user and linebackers drop back under both the shallow cross and the post, dump it down to the tight end on the chip-and-release route in the middle for 4 to 5 yards.

reads.label: 4th Read: Jet Motion Player
reads.text: If flat defenders are playing back and nothing is open downfield, throw to the jet motion player in the flat. Make one or two guys miss to pick up the first down.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side.
No other adjustments, run it stock.
plays.whenToUse: Run jet QB power and jet touch pass first, you have to establish that motion or this play does nothing. Once linebackers start jumping hard on that auto motion, that is your window. Call it in the red zone, on third down, or any time you see the defense selling out to stop the run.

plays.name: Corner Strike

reads.label: Cover 3: Seam Read
reads.text: The middle safety gets held by the slot streak. The backside corner gets held by the C route or comeback. Once the tight end clears the middle safety on his skinny post-seam, throw it up over the top down the seam for a big gain.

reads.label: Cover 2 / Two-High Shell
reads.text: Watch the linebacker depth. If he stays shallow, both the slot streak and the tight end seam come open. Go to whichever clears first.

reads.label: Man or Covered Deep: High-Low Backside
reads.text: If they are in man or the mid-safety takes away the deep options, work the backside high-low. Flat defender stays shallow, hit the C route as it breaks to the sideline. Flat defender plays back on the C route, check it down to the flat.

reads.label: Backside C Route vs. Man
reads.text: The streak and seam are not man-beaters. Against man coverage, rely on the C routes on either side of the field. Throw as the receiver breaks to the sideline.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side.
Middle slot on a streak.
Outside slot flat or whip, backside C route or comeback.
plays.whenToUse: Call this on third and long or any time you need a chunk play against zone. Cover 3 is the most common coverage you will face online, and this play is built specifically to carve it up. It is also solid against Cover 2 when that linebacker stays shallow. Keep it in your back pocket for fourth down too.

plays.name: MTN PA WR Zone Flood

reads.label: 1st Read: Corner Route (TE)
reads.text: As you boot out of the counter action, look for the tight end sneaking free on the corner route. The deep defender gets run off, the linebacker bites on the run fake, and the TE should be wide open. This is always the first option.

reads.label: 2nd Read: Shallow Cross (WR)
reads.text: If the corner is manned up or taken away, work to the shallow crosser. Against man, look for separation as he crosses the field. Against zone with linebackers biting or flowing to the corner, the crossing route opens underneath.

reads.label: 3rd Read: RB Flat
reads.text: Last option out of the pocket. If the corner is covered and the crosser is not available, the running back sneaks into the flat as the checkdown. A flat defender playing underneath creates the window as you roll out.

adjustments: Tight end to the wide side of the field.
No other adjustments, run it stock.
plays.whenToUse: Call this when defenses are selling out against the run or when linebackers are aggressive and bite hard on play action. The counter motion sets the whole thing up: they think run, you boot out and expose the backend. Works vs man or zone.

plays.name: MTN PA Corners

reads.label: 1st Read: TE Seam (The Money Route)
reads.text: Everything sells run: your gadget slot motions into the backfield and you run the ball a ton out of this exact look, so the linebackers come flying downhill. Behind them the tight end runs a really unique seam ball. Against Cover 3 he cuts inside the post safety while the backside deep third gets held out by the C route, and against Cover 2 he splits the two safeties. Drop it in over the top and you are off to the races.

reads.label: 2nd Read: The C Routes
reads.text: Against man this is the look: the seam is taken away, but the C routes break in and then snap hard back to the outside for big separation, and they work to either side of the field. Against zone, play the high-low: if the flat defender bites down on the motion man swinging out of the backfield, throw the C route breaking out right behind him.

reads.label: 3rd Read: Two Checkdowns
reads.text: If everything deep is covered or pressure is coming, you have two outlets: the running back in the flat to one side, and the motion receiver swinging to the short side on the other. Drop it to either one and let him work in the green grass.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side.
No other adjustments, run it stock.
plays.whenToUse: The fourth play off the same slot motion, with MTN WR Counter RT, MTN Triple Option RT, and MTN PA WR Zone Flood. The defense has watched that motion turn into runs all game, so the second the linebackers start flying downhill, call this and hit the tight end over the top. It beats Cover 3, splits Cover 2, and the C routes are your man-coverage answer.

plays.name: Y Shallow X Post

reads.label: Option Route (Behind the Mesh)
reads.text: This is a mesh concept with two drags underneath. If the linebackers and the user bite down on those drags, the option route comes in right behind them. Against zone he sits down and you fire it in. Against man he breaks it inside and gets really good separation.

reads.label: The Two Drags
reads.text: If they are in zone and everybody is playing off, just drop it down to either drag and let them get yards after the catch. Both are options against man too, just take whichever has more separation.

reads.label: RB Up the Seam
reads.text: The running back goes up the seam. If the linebackers and the user stay down on the drags, or jump over to take away the option route, that back gets to such a nice area of the field and you can fire it in there for big plays.

reads.label: Out Route
reads.text: If that flat defender or the short-side corner gets sucked inside by the back on the seam, the out route is breaking out to the sideline at about fifteen yards.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field.
Running back on a streak.
Outside receiver on the wide side on a drag.
plays.whenToUse: This is a true star play because it answers everything. The mesh occupies the underneath defenders, the option route sits behind them versus zone and separates versus man, and the back up the seam punishes anyone who squats on the drags. When they collapse the middle, the out route breaks wide open on the boundary.

plays.name: RPO Pin Alert Bubble

reads.label: Numbers Advantage
reads.text: Count defenders to the bubble side. If there are only two defenders outside, you already have your two blockers accounted for, throw the bubble every single time.

reads.label: Defender Cheats Inside
reads.text: If the third defender is present but jumps inside or plays a hook zone at the snap, that creates a one-on-one on the outside, throw the bubble and make one miss for easy yardage.

reads.label: User / LB Jumps to Bubble
reads.text: If a defender aggressively crashes outside toward the bubble at the snap, pull the ball and hand off. Multiple pullers are already working across the formation, plant and cut upfield for 8 to 10 yards.

reads.label: Three Defenders Outside
reads.text: If the defense has three guys to the bubble side and one shoots outside at the snap, hand it off automatically. The pullers will outnumber the pursuit, cut back inside if defenders overrun.

adjustments: Bubble always to the wide side.
Multiple pulling guards backside.
Cut back inside on overrun.
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you want to put the defense in a conflict. If they give you numbers outside, you are throwing the bubble. If they try to take it away, you are handing it off with pullers. They cannot have it both ways, that is why this play is in the bag.

plays.name: RPO Glance Bubble

reads.label: Bubble Read
reads.text: Pre-snap, eye the overhang defender over the bubble. If he crashes inside at the snap or is already shaded inside giving you a numbers advantage, two-on-one or three-on-two, throw the bubble. One blocker to beat on the outside.

reads.label: Handoff Read
reads.text: If the overhang does not crash and your eyes were set on the bubble side, check the backside defenders. If both defenders are staying back on the slant side, that is your downhill run key, hand it off and get skinny through the hole.

reads.label: Slant Read
reads.text: If pre-snap you choose to key the slant, confirm the corner is in off coverage, avoid inside shaded press. Then watch the linebackers and any hole safety. If they bite down, fire the slant in behind them.

reads.label: Pre-Snap Commitment
reads.text: You must pick your primary read side before the snap, bubble side or slant side. Your eye discipline determines whether you are reading the bubble and run or the slant and run.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side.
Backside slant stem down one notch.
plays.whenToUse: Run this when defenses are loading the box. Spread to run: if they give you the box, you take the outside. This play punishes every defensive adjustment: crash down, you bubble; play the pass, you run it; split the middle, you slant. It is a built-in answer for whatever they give you.
